See the code: https://github.com/BrianS3/gas_forecasting/blob/main/R/gas_forecasting_process.R

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)
source(here("R", "gas_data_prep.R"))
library(plotly)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, out.width = "100%")

dollars <- function(x) paste0("$", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2))

# results written by gas_forecasting_process.R
con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), here("database", "gas_data.db"))
projection         <- dbGetQuery(con, "select * from forecast_two_month")
projection_monthly <- dbGetQuery(con, "select * from forecast_monthly") %>% mutate(month = as.Date(month))
backtest           <- dbGetQuery(con, "select * from forecast_backtest") %>% mutate(start_month = as.Date(start_month))
accuracy           <- dbGetQuery(con, "select * from forecast_accuracy")
dbDisconnect(con)

model_names <- c(naive = "Naive (last month carries forward)",
                 ets   = "ETS (exponential smoothing)",
                 arima = "ARIMA (on log price)")

start_month <- as.Date(projection$start_month)
end_month   <- as.Date(projection$end_month)

# any weeks already in for the projected months
so_far <- gas_weekly %>%
  filter(date >= start_month) %>%
  summarise(weeks = n(), avg = mean(price))
```

# 2-month projection

The U.S. national average is projected to be **`r dollars(projection$projected)` per gallon** on average for
**`r format(start_month, "%B")` – `r format(end_month, "%B %Y")`**.

The likely range is **`r dollars(projection$lower_80)` to `r dollars(projection$upper_80)`** (80% interval:
in 8 out of 10 simulated outcomes, the 2-month average landed in this range).

| Month | Projected | Likely range (80%) |
|---|---|---|
`r paste0("| ", format(projection_monthly$month, "%B %Y"), " | ", dollars(projection_monthly$projected), " | ", dollars(projection_monthly$lower_80), " – ", dollars(projection_monthly$upper_80), " |", collapse = "\n")`

`r if (so_far$weeks > 0) paste0("**So far:** ", so_far$weeks, " week(s) of ", format(start_month, "%B"), " are in, averaging ", dollars(so_far$avg), ".") else ""`

Model used: **`r model_names[projection$model]`**, the model with the smallest miss in the backtest below.
Projections use complete months through `r format(as.Date(projection$last_actual_month), "%B %Y")`.

```{r projection chart, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
recent <- gas_monthly %>% filter(month >= start_month - years(3))

projection_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = projection_monthly,
              aes(x = month, ymin = lower_80, ymax = upper_80), fill = "#2F855A", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = recent,
            aes(x = month, y = price, group = 1,
                text = paste0(format(month, "%B %Y"), " actual: ", dollars(price))),
            color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = bind_rows(tail(recent, 1) %>% rename(projected = price), projection_monthly),
            aes(x = month, y = projected, group = 1), color = "#2F855A", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = projection_monthly,
             aes(x = month, y = projected,
                 text = paste0(format(month, "%B %Y"), " projected: ", dollars(projected),
                               "<br>Range: ", dollars(lower_80), " - ", dollars(upper_80))),
             color = "#2F855A", size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b '%y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Monthly national average: actual (black) and projected (green)", x = "", y = "Dollars per gallon")

ggplotly(projection_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

# How good has this been?

To check the method, we went back to each of the last `r nrow(backtest) / nrow(accuracy)` months, pretended
it was that month, projected the next 2-month average, and compared it to what actually happened.

```{r accuracy table}
accuracy %>%
  transmute(Model = model_names[model],
            `Average miss` = dollars(avg_miss_dollars),
            `Bias` = paste0(ifelse(avg_bias_dollars >= 0, "+", "-"), dollars(abs(avg_bias_dollars))),
            `Windows tested` = windows_tested) %>%
  kable(align = "lrrr")
```

*Average miss* is how far off the 2-month average was, on average. *Bias* is the typical direction:
negative means the projections ran low (prices came in higher than projected).

```{r backtest chart, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
best_backtest <- backtest %>% filter(model == projection$model)

backtest_plot <- ggplot(best_backtest, aes(x = start_month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = actual, color = "Actual 2-month average", group = 1,
                text = paste0(format(start_month, "%b %Y"), " + next month<br>Actual: ", dollars(actual))),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = projected, color = "Projected 2 months earlier", group = 1,
                text = paste0(format(start_month, "%b %Y"), " + next month<br>Projected: ", dollars(projected),
                              "<br>Miss: ", dollars(error))),
            linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual 2-month average" = "grey20", "Projected 2 months earlier" = "#2F855A")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b '%y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Backtest: what the model projected vs. what happened", x = "2-month window starting", y = "", color = "")

ggplotly(backtest_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

**Limits.** These models only look at past prices. They can't see a war, a hurricane, or an OPEC decision
coming, so sudden shocks (like the jump in March 2026) show up as big misses. Treat the projection as
"where prices are heading if nothing major changes."
